heartbeat.title: Specific, forward-looking subject lines beat static framing
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest pattern across August's wins is that concrete, forward-looking angles outperform warm but generic messaging. Site Abandon won by leading with an expiring, named discount cue, Post-Purchase won by teasing what the customer can expect next, and Product Onboarding won with a direct, personal directive before the first use. The transferable lesson is that subscribers respond to messages that answer their most immediate question, whether that is "what happens next?" or "why act now?", and we are rolling that framing across more flows. This is the compounding logic of the testing programme: each win is banked permanently into the flows, while the tests that do not win cost nothing, so the whole system keeps improving regardless of any single result.

narrative.html: Flows reached 35.0% of total store revenue, up from 19.6% last month and the highest point in the 12-month series. Even though flow revenue eased slightly to 29,667 EUR (down 9.1%), flows captured a far larger slice of a smaller total, which shows they held their ground while overall store demand softened.

Flow revenue per email delivered was 0.218 EUR, down from 0.439 EUR last month. This is worth watching, though the drop reflects list volume and send mix more than flow quality, and flows remain the most efficient per-email channel we run.

Flows earn 3.2x more per email than campaigns (0.218 EUR vs 0.068 EUR), and made up 63% of email revenue from a lean 8 campaign sends. Flows are our most efficient lever, and campaigns are the second lever we run alongside them to add reach on top of the automated base.

Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.453% of delivered and spam complaints at just 0.016%. Healthy list hygiene keeps both flows and campaigns landing in the inbox and protects the sender reputation the whole programme depends on.

monthly.title_sub: Flows delivered 29,667 EUR in August and reached 35.0% of total store revenue, their highest share of the year.

heartbeat.title: Emotional continuity beats generic reminders
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest lesson from this month's winners is that messaging tied to the customer's own progress and feelings outperforms neutral, discount-led copy. Progress-protection framing on Site Abandon and a comfort-focused emotional payoff on Browse Abandon both won, confirming that reinforcing why staying consistent matters drives more opens than generic subscribe-and-save or reminder language. We are carrying that principle into the next round of tests across the flows.

narrative.html: Flows delivered 32,646 EUR, a slight dip of 3.5% versus last month, but their share of total store revenue climbed to 19.6%, up from 14.4% in June and the strongest reading since October. Flows are pulling a bigger slice of everything the store sells.

Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run. At 0.439 EUR revenue per email delivered, they earn 4.1x what our campaigns return per email (0.106 EUR). This is why the automated flows carry the bulk of the load between sends.

Flow RPR eased to 0.439 EUR from 0.559 EUR. The share of store revenue is up while per-email yield softened, which points to volume and store demand doing more of the work this month. We are watching this to keep the per-email return firm.

Campaigns are the second lever we run, with 10 sent this month, giving a near-even split of email revenue (flows 49%). Deliverability stayed clean, with unsubscribes at 0.571% of delivered and spam complaints at just 0.043%.

monthly.title_sub: Flows held at 32,646 EUR and lifted to 19.6% of total store revenue this month.
